title: Structuring Singapore for Flourishing Families
what_it_is: A Member's speech in Parliament setting out proposals on family support, leave entitlements, childcare subsidies and childcare access.
why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.
not_said: Whether the Government will raise the statutory minimum annual leave or by how much
Whether employees will be permitted to use their own sick leave for dependants' medical certificates
Whether childcare leave days for children aged 0-7 and 8-12 will be increased
Whether childcare subsidies will be made universal regardless of the mother's employment status
What the outcome of the review of leave policies is
what_happens_next: The Government is developing a long-term roadmap and will study Ms Chen's suggestions as part of the Workgroup; it is also exploring more support for returning parents and more protected time for working parents.

key_points.point: The statutory minimum annual leave under section 88A of the Employment Act is seven days, rising by one day per year up to a cap of 14 years.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: Presently, the statutory minimum annual leave under section 88A of the Employment Act is seven days, increasing by one each year, up to a cap of 14 years.
